raw_text: Tomato late blight is caused by Phytophthora infestans, an oomycete pathogen. Early symptoms: small dark water-soaked spots on leaves; pale green lesions that expand quickly. Late symptoms: brown lesions on stems; white sporulation on leaf undersides in wet weather. Conditions: 10 to 25 C, high humidity, wet leaves, cool weather. Environment: poor airflow; rain. The disease can be severe and rapidly destroy foliage. Organic treatment: copper. Chemical treatment: chlorothalonil. Prevention: remove volunteer tomato plants; avoid overhead irrigation; improve air circulation.
